title: Interactive and Experiential Art
answer: Audience-reactive installations, generative AR and VR, dialogue engines, data sculptures and audio-visual systems.

children.name: Audience-Reactive Installations
children.blurb: Audience-reactive installations are artworks that change in response to the presence, movement, sound, or other signals from viewers.

children.name: Generative AR and VR Environments
children.blurb: Generative AR and VR environments are real-time, interactive spaces where procedural or model-driven content creates or alters the world around a viewer.

children.name: Dialogue Engines and Virtual Docents
children.blurb: Dialogue engines and virtual docents are interactive artworks that use conversational AI to act as guides, narrators, or interlocutors in galleries, museums, and public spaces.

children.name: Data Sculpture
children.blurb: Data sculpture is an art practice that turns datasets, sensor streams, or model outputs into physical or spatial forms.

children.name: Audio-Visual Systems
children.blurb: Audio-visual systems in interactive and experiential art are installations and performances where sound and moving image respond to each other, to the space, or to audience input in real time.

sections.body: Interactive and experiential art uses AI to make works that respond to people, places, or data in real time. Right now this means installations that change based on movement or sound, virtual spaces generated as someone explores them, and systems that hold a conversation with a visitor. Artists also build physical objects that reshape themselves from live information and audio-visual setups where machine learning drives both sound and image. The AI is not just a tool for making a fixed piece, it is part of the work while the work is running.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field is active but uneven. Audience-reactive installations and audio-visual systems are the most mature, with reliable sensors and models that can run on modest hardware in a gallery. Generative AR and VR still struggle with latency and visual consistency, so many pieces feel like prototypes rather than finished environments. Dialogue engines can hold short, engaging exchanges but often lose the thread or repeat themselves, and data sculptures are limited by the cost and fragility of physical actuators. Honest limits include unpredictable behavior in public spaces, high power use, and the fact that many works only function well under controlled lighting or sound conditions.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader who wants to understand physical spaces that sense people should start with Audience-Reactive Installations, which covers the core techniques of tracking and response. Generative AR and VR Environments extends that into worlds viewed through headsets or phones, while Dialogue Engines and Virtual Docents looks at works that speak with visitors instead of just reacting to them. Data Sculpture moves from screens and projections to physical objects driven by live feeds, and Audio-Visual Systems ties together the sound and image side, where many of the 2000 audio models tracked on this site find artistic use. Together the five pages move from room scale interaction to wearable and conversational forms, then to material objects and combined media.
